pull.title: fix: recover orphan job publication PaymentIntent creation
pull.body:
## Summary
- move job-publication PaymentIntent creation out of the pessimistic database transaction
- persist a durable creation claim before calling Stripe, then attach the authoritative provider id in a second short transaction
- recover the crash window where Stripe created the PaymentIntent but the process died before `stripe_payment_intent_id` was stored
- replay the exact stable Stripe idempotency key only within a conservative 23-hour safety window; after that, fail closed to manual review instead of risking a duplicate PaymentIntent
- add bounded attempts, two-minute leases, retry/backoff and multi-instance-safe pessimistic claims
- if cancellation races with provider creation, attach the recovered intent and immediately hand it to the durable V56 cleanup queue
- preserve signed-webhook authority for late successful payments; recovery never publishes or resurrects a cancelled job
- add Flyway V57, state/recovery/scheduler/flow tests, and a real PostgreSQL schema smoke wired into the job-publication payment workflow

## Crash window closed
Previously `PaymentIntent.create()` ran while the publication row was locked. A process crash after Stripe accepted creation but before the local transaction committed could leave an orphan provider PaymentIntent with no local id. If the publication later expired or was cancelled, cleanup could not address that provider object.

The new flow is `prepare/claim DB -> Stripe outside transaction -> finalize DB`. A durable `stripe_create_started_at` marker proves creation work started. If the provider id was lost by a crash, the recovery worker replays the same request under the same idempotency key while that replay is still safe, recovers the provider id, and converges cancelled rows into the existing V56 cleanup mechanism.

## Safety properties
- no database row lock spans a Stripe create/retrieve call
- no automatic replay after the conservative provider idempotency window
- no replay for historical cancelled rows that predate V57 because they have no durable create-start marker
- provider identity, amount, currency and metadata are validated before attaching the id
- concurrent app instances cannot both claim the same creation/recovery lease
- late successful Stripe payments remain webhook-authoritative and never resurrect a cancelled publication

## Migration
- V57 `job_publication_payment_intent_create_recovery`

## Merge gate
Merge only after exact-head API/Web/Compose/CodeQL and relevant runtime/payment smokes are green, master is unchanged from the PR base, the PR is mergeable and 0 commits behind, using merge commit with expected head SHA.
